text:
natalie_support: FYI customer on a private VPC is seeing streaming resets for inference requests. TLS completes, then stream RST ~10-30s in. Happening from their on-prem NAT -> our private endpoint. Escalating to infra/networking. Captured tcpdump. Any ideas?

sanjay: can you paste `conntrack -L | wc -l` from their NAT box and `ss -tn state TIME-WAIT`? Also need NAT pool size and SNAT rotation rate.

natalie_support: got snippets, pasted below.

`conntrack -L | head -n 5`

```
tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.0.0.5 dst=18.197.23.11 sport=54321 dport=443 ...
... many TIME_WAIT entries
```

NAT pool is 2 EIPs rotating, ~1000 ephemeral ports each.

mike_net: looks like SNAT pool is too small. Also check their NACLs — remember NACLs are stateless: you need an explicit egress allow for ephemeral ports. If egress denies that range, return traffic can get dropped even though SG allows 443. Are their NACL rules only allowing 443 with a following deny?

natalie_support: yes their SG allows outbound 443 but the NACL outbound list shows only `allow 443` then `deny all`. snippet:

```
# NACL outbound
100: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0
110: DENY ALL 0.0.0.0/0
```

They didn't include ephemeral ranges.

infra-bot: probe-run: started TCP probes from their NAT EIP -> our inference endpoint.
Result: 100/200 succeeded when ephemeral port < 61000, failures when ephemeral > 61000. Failures show `RST` from mid-path.

kevin_ops: recommendation checklist:
- Add NACL outbound rule to allow ephemeral ports 32768-65535 to inference subnets (rule number between existing allow and deny)
- Or increase SNAT pool (more EIPs) so ephemeral port reuse drops
- If security policy allows, prefer stateful SGs for egress so return traffic is handled automatically
- For immediate test: add a temporary broad egress allow on the NACL to 0.0.0.0/0 ports 32768-65535 and confirm streaming stability

Quick command (example):
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-xxxx --rule-number 105 --protocol tcp --port-range From=32768,To=65535 --egress --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
```

Also check conntrack size on their NAT device and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` — if conntrack table is filling you will see SYN retries and mid-flow RSTs.

natalie_support: i'll send the change to the customer as a test and report back. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
